youtube.title: Why Is the Donbas Front Line Stuck?
youtube.description:
Much of the front line in Donbas has barely moved since 2023, even after years of fighting and huge armies on both sides. Why is it so hard to push the line, and what keeps it where it is?

This video follows the map: the flat steppe, the rivers, ridges and slag heaps, the drones that watch every field, and the borders drawn here since a Welsh industrialist began the steelworks that grew into Donetsk in 1869. It sets out what Russia and Ukraine each say they want, in their own words, and three ways the line on the map could change.

{CHAPTERS}

sources.claim: about 1,200 kilometres of active front
sources.source: Ukraine's Armed Forces commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi, public statements 2024-2025

sources.claim: Russian forces gained 4,000 to 4,300 square kilometres in 2024, ISW and DeepState estimate
sources.source: DeepState (Ukrainian open-source mapping project), annual summary, January 2025: about 4,300 km²; Institute for the Study of War, end-of-2024 assessment: about 4,000 km²

sources.claim: less than one percent of Ukraine
sources.source: 4,000-4,300 km² against Ukraine's area of 603,550 km² (State Statistics Service of Ukraine): about 0.7%

sources.claim: in 2025 NATO pledged 5 percent of GDP to defence and security, citing Russia
sources.source: NATO, The Hague Summit Declaration, 25 June 2025: 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defence, 1.5% defence- and security-related), citing 'the long-term threat posed by Russia to Euro-Atlantic security'

sources.claim: Donbas usually means Donetsk and Luhansk regions, plus fringes of their neighbours
sources.source: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, 'Donets Basin' (the basin also reaches into Dnipropetrovsk region and Russia's Rostov region)

sources.claim: Donetsk and Luhansk cover about 53,000 square kilometres
sources.source: State Statistics Service of Ukraine: Donetsk oblast 26,517 km², Luhansk oblast 26,684 km²

sources.claim: a little larger than Costa Rica
sources.source: Costa Rica area 51,100 km², CIA World Factbook

sources.claim: about six and a half million people lived here before 2014
sources.source: State Statistics Service of Ukraine, population on 1 January 2014: Donetsk 4.34 million, Luhansk 2.24 million

sources.claim: about 15 percent of Ukraine's economy in 2013
sources.source: State Statistics Service of Ukraine, gross regional product by region, 2013

sources.claim: by late 2025 Russian forces held nearly all of Luhansk and most of Donetsk
sources.source: Institute for the Study of War (ISW) campaign assessment maps, late 2025

sources.claim: Donetsk to Kramatorsk about 80 kilometres in a straight line
sources.source: Great-circle distance between city centres (about 82 km)

sources.claim: Donets Ridge, across the centre and east of Donbas, low hills under 370 metres
sources.source: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, 'Donets Ridge': highest point Mohyla Mechetna, 367 m

sources.claim: coal mining left tall slag heaps
sources.source: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, 'Donets Basin'

sources.claim: Ukraine built more than 1.5 million drones in 2024
sources.source: Ukraine's Ministry of Strategic Industries and Ministry of Defence, statements January-February 2025

sources.claim: a strip about 10 to 15 kilometres deep where almost anything that moves is seen and targeted
sources.source: RUSI, Watling and Reynolds, 'Tactical Developments During the Third Year of the Russo-Ukrainian War', February 2025

sources.claim: tanks and trucks struggle to cross that strip
sources.source: RUSI, Watling and Reynolds, February 2025

sources.claim: in 1869 John Hughes began building a steelworks
sources.source: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, 'Hughes, John' and 'Donetsk'; New Russia Company founded 1869

sources.claim: Yuzovka, later Stalino, renamed Donetsk in 1961
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Donetsk'

sources.claim: in 1924 and 1925 Taganrog and Shakhty went to Russia
sources.source: Hiroaki Kuromiya, 'Freedom and Terror in the Donbas', Cambridge University Press, 1998

sources.claim: Soviet planners lined the fields with windbreaks of trees
sources.source: USSR Council of Ministers decree of 20 October 1948 on field-protective forest belts (the 'Great Plan for the Transformation of Nature')

sources.claim: 57 percent Ukrainian and 38 percent Russian in Donetsk region, 2001
sources.source: All-Ukrainian Population Census 2001: Ukrainians 56.9%, Russians 38.2%

sources.claim: three in four people in Donetsk region named Russian as their native language in 2001
sources.source: All-Ukrainian Population Census 2001: 74.9%

sources.claim: about 84 percent of voters in both regions backed independence in December 1991
sources.source: Central Election Commission results, 1 December 1991 referendum: Donetsk 83.9%, Luhansk 83.9%

sources.claim: protests in Kyiv toppled President Viktor Yanukovych, who fled to Russia, early 2014
sources.source: BBC, Reuters reporting, February 2014

sources.claim: in April 2014 armed separatists seized government buildings in Sloviansk, Donetsk and Luhansk
sources.source: OSCE and Reuters reporting, April 2014

sources.claim: Ukraine and Western governments said Russia armed and led them; Moscow denied sending troops
sources.source: NATO and US State Department statements 2014; Kremlin statements 2014

sources.claim: Minsk deals of 2014 and 2015 set a line of contact about 500 kilometres long
sources.source: Minsk Protocol, 5 September 2014; Package of Measures (Minsk II), 12 February 2015; OSCE Special Monitoring Mission to Ukraine, reports 2015-2021

sources.claim: OSCE monitors logged ceasefire violations along the line almost every day
sources.source: OSCE Special Monitoring Mission to Ukraine, daily reports 2015-2021

sources.claim: more than 14,000 people killed there by early 2022
sources.source: UN OHCHR, conflict-related casualties in Ukraine, January 2022: 14,200-14,400 deaths, 14 April 2014 - 31 December 2021

sources.claim: on 24 February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion
sources.source: UN Secretary-General statements; Kremlin address, 24 February 2022

sources.claim: Russian forces pulled back from around Kyiv within weeks
sources.source: Ukraine Ministry of Defence and ISW, early April 2022

sources.claim: by early July 2022 Russia had taken Sievierodonetsk and Lysychansk
sources.source: Ukrainian General Staff confirmation of withdrawal, 25 June and 3 July 2022

sources.claim: Ukraine retook most of Kharkiv region and, on 1 October, Lyman
sources.source: Ukrainian Ministry of Defence; Russian Ministry of Defence statement, 1 October 2022

sources.claim: in September 2022 Russia held votes in occupied areas and declared four regions annexed
sources.source: Kremlin, 30 September 2022; votes held 23-27 September 2022

sources.claim: on 12 October 2022 the UN General Assembly rejected the annexation by 143 votes to 5
sources.source: UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/ES-11/4, 12 October 2022 (143 for, 5 against, 35 abstentions)

sources.claim: on the UN's own maps all four regions are still drawn inside Ukraine's borders
sources.source: UN Geospatial Information Section, map of Ukraine; UN GA resolution ES-11/4 calls on states not to recognise any alteration of Ukraine's borders

sources.claim: Russian forces dug belts of trenches, anti-tank ditches and minefields over the winter
sources.source: RUSI, Watling and Reynolds, 'Stormbreak', September 2023

sources.claim: when Ukraine attacked in June 2023 it freed only a handful of villages
sources.source: RUSI 'Stormbreak', September 2023; ISW assessments, autumn 2023

sources.claim: the battle for Bakhmut lasted about ten months, until Russia claimed it in May 2023
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Defence claim, 20 May 2023; ISW, August 2022 - May 2023

sources.claim: in February 2024 Ukraine withdrew from Avdiivka, about 15 kilometres north of central Donetsk
sources.source: Ukraine commander-in-chief statement, 17 February 2024; distance between centres

sources.claim: the front crept about 40 kilometres west to the edges of Pokrovsk
sources.source: ISW maps, February 2024 - January 2025; distance Avdiivka to Pokrovsk

sources.claim: Russia's constitution lists Donetsk and Luhansk as Russian regions
sources.source: Constitution of the Russian Federation, Article 65, as amended by federal constitutional laws of 4 October 2022

sources.claim: Moscow says Yanukovych was removed unconstitutionally; Putin: 'an anti-constitutional takeover, an armed seizure of power'
sources.source: Kremlin transcript, Vladimir Putin answers journalists' questions on the situation in Ukraine, 4 March 2014 (kremlin.ru)

sources.claim: Moscow says the May 2014 referendums and the September 2022 votes expressed the will of local people
sources.source: Kremlin statement, 12 May 2014 ('Moscow respects the will of the population of Donetsk and Lugansk regions'); Kremlin address, 30 September 2022

sources.claim: Putin: the people of these regions have become our citizens, forever
sources.source: Kremlin transcript, address of 30 September 2022 (kremlin.ru)

sources.claim: Moscow says Kyiv never fully carried out the Minsk deals, including special status for Donbas
sources.source: Minsk II, 12 February 2015, points 4 and 11 (special status, constitutional reform); Kremlin address, 21 February 2022; Russian Foreign Ministry statements 2015-2022

sources.claim: Moscow's stated security reasons: protecting people in Donbas and keeping NATO from its borders
sources.source: Kremlin transcript, address of 24 February 2022; Russian draft security treaty proposals, 17 December 2021

sources.claim: Kyiv says the 2022 votes were held under occupation without independent observers
sources.source: Ukraine Ministry of Foreign Affairs statements, September 2022; UN GA resolution ES-11/4

sources.claim: Budapest Memorandum: respect the independence and sovereignty and the existing borders of Ukraine
sources.source: Memorandum on Security Assurances, Budapest, 5 December 1994, paragraph 1

sources.claim: Ukraine's constitution: territory changes only by an all-Ukrainian referendum
sources.source: Constitution of Ukraine, Article 73

sources.claim: Kyiv says foreign forces never left and Ukraine never regained its border, as Minsk promised
sources.source: Minsk II, 12 February 2015, points 9 and 10; Ukraine Ministry of Foreign Affairs statements 2015-2022

sources.claim: Russia spent about 149 billion dollars and Ukraine 65 billion on their militaries in 2024
sources.source: SIPRI, 'Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2024', April 2025

sources.claim: Ukraine's military spending was about 34 percent of its economy
sources.source: SIPRI, April 2025

sources.claim: analysts call the northern Donetsk cities Ukraine's fortress belt
sources.source: Institute for the Study of War, assessment of Russia's demand for the rest of Donetsk Oblast, August 2025

sources.claim: about 190 kilometres from Kramatorsk to Dnipro
sources.source: Great-circle distance between city centres

sources.claim: Pokrovsk held Ukraine's only coking coal mine, halted by Metinvest in January 2025
sources.source: Metinvest statement, 14 January 2025; Reuters, January 2025

sources.claim: on 15 August 2025 Trump met Putin in Anchorage, Alaska; no ceasefire was agreed
sources.source: Reuters, AP, 15-16 August 2025

sources.claim: Russia asked Ukraine to leave the rest of Donetsk in return for freezing other fronts
sources.source: Reuters, 21 August 2025, citing sources familiar with the talks; not confirmed by the Kremlin

sources.claim: Zelensky, days before the summit: Ukrainians will not gift their land to the occupier
sources.source: Volodymyr Zelensky, video address, 9 August 2025

sources.claim: in November 2025 a US draft plan proposed a demilitarised zone in that area
sources.source: Axios and Reuters, 20-21 November 2025

sources.claim: Korea's armistice line, 1953, about 250 kilometres long
sources.source: Korean Armistice Agreement, 27 July 1953; DMZ length about 248 km (Encyclopaedia Britannica)

sources.claim: Ukraine's front nearly five times longer than Korea's line
sources.source: About 1,200 km (Syrskyi) against about 248 km (Britannica): 4.8 times

sources.claim: Kramatorsk and Sloviansk home to more than 250,000 people before the war
sources.source: State Statistics Service of Ukraine, population 1 January 2022: Kramatorsk about 147,000, Sloviansk about 105,000

sources.claim: analysts say Ukraine's next line would sit on open farmland with fewer hills and towns
sources.source: Institute for the Study of War, assessment of Russia's demand for the rest of Donetsk Oblast, August 2025

sources.claim: Kyiv says giving up those cities would hand Russia a springboard for the next attack
sources.source: Volodymyr Zelensky, remarks to reporters, 12 August 2025

sources.claim: about 60 kilometres from Pokrovsk to Kramatorsk
sources.source: Great-circle distance between city centres

sources.claim: analysts at RUSI say either side could break through if the other runs short of soldiers, shells or air defence
sources.source: RUSI, Watling and Reynolds, February 2025 (analysis, not forecast)
